campbell.title: Campbell City Council — August 18, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered several administrative and staffing items, including choosing voting delegates for the upcoming League of California Cities annual conference and amending an agreement covering city clerk services. The Council also considered accepting a grant on behalf of the police department, with a presentation from the police captain, and took up a governance-related update on the BART Silicon Valley project.
keyTopics: Selection of voting delegates for the 2026 League of California Cities annual conference
Resolution amending the first amended agreement for city clerk services
Grant acceptance on behalf of the police department, presented by the police captain
Update on governance related to the BART Silicon Valley project

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council reviewed routine items like meeting minutes, vendor payments, and the Treasurer's Report, and considered draft responses to two Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's oversight of the BART Silicon Valley Phase II project. The Council also took up several policy items, including support for a state data transparency bill, a contract for a transportation impact fee study, forming a committee to look at alternative policing services, and the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival.
keyTopics: Draft responses to Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's management of BART Silicon Valley Phase II
Support for AB 1761, which addresses data transparency for utility rate charges
An $85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an Ad-Hoc Committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
The future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and continued involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — August 25, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered several infrastructure and housing items, including a roof replacement contract for the History Museum, an EV charger installation project at the Maintenance Yard, and completion of the Woodland Library patio expansion. The Council also held a public hearing on a resident petition to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street, and reviewed two large condominium development proposals on First Street and near Sherwood and Acacia Avenues.
keyTopics: Public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Vesting tentative maps for new condominium projects at 349 First Street (19 units) and Sherwood/Acacia Avenues (33 units)
History Museum roof replacement contract with Diablo Roofing, not to exceed $147,500 plus 15% contingency
Maintenance Yard EV Chargers construction contract with Bockmon & Woody Electric Co., not to exceed $363,220
Draft responses to County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's BART Silicon Valley Phase II oversight

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 1, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council met to approve routine meeting minutes and take up a handful of housekeeping and administrative items. Topics included vacating a public service easement on Cerro Vista, setting up preferential and time-limited parking in a specific area, and hiring an outside consultant to help with executive-level work.
keyTopics: Vacating a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista
Establishing preferential permit parking and time-limited parking
Authorizing a consultant agreement for executive-related services
Approval of minutes from several August 2026 Council meetings

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 2, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the draft agenda for the September 15, 2026 meeting, including whether to add new items, assign specific times to agenda items, or note any waiver requirements. The committee also considered the City Clerk's public record for August 20–27, 2026, and a study session on infrastructure financing tools for economic development.
keyTopics: Review and adjustments to the September 15, 2026 draft agenda, including new items and time assignments
Public record report from the City Clerk covering August 20–27, 2026
Study session on infrastructure financing tools for economic development

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — August 31, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's Youth Advisory Committee met to take public comments, do a team-building exercise, and go over the basic rules that govern how the committee operates. Members also discussed their role on the committee and began brainstorming ideas for their work plan for the upcoming fiscal year.
keyTopics: Public comments during oral communications
Team-building activity for committee members
Overview of the Brown Act and Robert's Rules of Order
Discussion of the Youth Advisory Committee's role
Brainstorming for the FY 2026-27 work plan

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting on August 25, 2026, that began with a closed session, followed by a separate public meeting focused on a presentation. The public portion centered on an update regarding the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session held at 4:30 p.m.
CleanWater Program update presentation at the 6 p.m. special meeting

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 1, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council held a closed session and reported out on it in open session. The meeting also included a public notice about the city's lobbyist registration and reporting requirements, clarifying who is and isn't required to register under the local lobbying ordinance.
keyTopics: Report from closed session
Lobbyist registration and reporting requirements under Cupertino's lobbying ordinance

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, allowing both in-person attendance and remote participation via Zoom or phone. One council member, Boardmember Chahal, participated remotely from India. The agenda excerpt provided does not include details on specific policy items discussed.
keyTopics: Hybrid meeting format with in-person and remote (Zoom/phone) participation options for the public
Boardmember Chahal participated remotely from Panchkula, India

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 1, 2026
milpitas.summary: The City Council, sitting as the board of the Successor Agency to the former Redevelopment Agency, considered routine financial and administrative business. This included confirming which city officials hold official roles on the Successor Agency and authorizing the sale of bonds to refinance existing redevelopment-related debt.
keyTopics: Confirming and designating city officials as officers of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Authorizing issuance and sale of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance existing Successor Agency debt

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Economic Development Committee — August 26, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Economic Development Committee reviewed a proposed strategy for retaining, expanding, and attracting local businesses, and received a staff update on economic development activity for August 2026. The meeting focused on presentations rather than final decisions.
keyTopics: Staff presentation on the Business Retention, Expansion, and Attraction (BRE/A) Strategy
Economic Development Activity Report for August 2026
